notes: Fifty-fourth annual report of the Board of Park Commissioners (1924), edited by Clay M. Greene, covering the years since 1912. Curated: the de Young Memorial Museum's building and dedication, Kezar Stadium.

coverage.remaining: Not placed (no page): Fleishhacker Pool and its bathhouse by Ward & Blohme, the Fleishhacker Mothers' House, Aquatic Park (Bakewell, Brown & Bauer), the Harding Park clubhouse by George W. Kelham, the Legion of Honor's dedication on November 11, 1924, the Marina yacht harbor.

findings.description: M. H. de Young submitted plans for a new Memorial Museum to the Park Commission on September 1, 1916; they were accepted, the cornerstone was laid on April 15, 1917, and building of the first unit began at once.

citation.label: Annual report of the Board of Park Commissioners of San Francisco for the year ending June 30, 1924, Memorial Museum

findings.description: Before ten thousand people the new museum was dedicated on January 2, 1921, after de Young handed the Park Commission the deed of trust placing it and its contents in the commissioners' keeping as a museum free to the people forever; he gave it on the one condition that it never be closed and never charge admission.

findings.description: Kezar Stadium was built with Mary A. Kezar's $100,000 bequest and $100,000 from the city, on land leased from the street railway company on Lincoln Way and on the park's old nursery, stable and shop grounds: plans by Willis Polk & Company with Geoffrey Bangs, Thomas F. Chase, C. F. Masten and Lester W. Hurd, and the contract to Palmer & McBryde, to be finished in 100 working days. The concrete bowl seated 22,000 to begin with and was named for her.
